policy.reviewer_gate: Independent domain reviewer must validate source scope, exact product/build, prerequisites, applicability, remediation safety, validation and rollback before any candidate can become an approved KnowledgeEntry.
policy.stale_policy: No review interval assigned. Trigger revalidation on vendor revision, product EOL/support change, security advisory, product-version drift, failed usage outcome or contradictory incident evidence.

candidates.version_scope: Windows Server 2008+ per event reference; verify OS build and event schema version
candidates.title: An account failed to log on
candidates.applicability: Only when Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing Event ID 4625 is present on the computer where the logon attempt occurred.
prerequisites: Verify effective Audit Logon failure policy and Security log retention; do not assume event coverage.
limitations: 4625 proves a failed logon, not its root cause by itself.
Interpret Status/SubStatus with LogonType and source context.
Event is generated on the computer where the logon was attempted.
next_checks: Correlate repeated failures by account, source host/IP, logon type and time.
Check account state and relevant domain-controller events before changing credentials or policy.
validation: Perform an authorized controlled sign-in and confirm expected success/failure event sequence and source context.
Confirm unexpected repeated failures stop in an agreed observation window.
rollback: No change prescribed by this source. Revert only a separately approved audit-policy change to the recorded pre-change policy.

candidates.version_scope: Windows Server family; verify OS and event schema
candidates.title: A user account was locked out
candidates.applicability: Only when Event ID 4740 exists for the affected account; source describes user-account lockout events on DCs, member servers and workstations.
prerequisites: Verify effective Audit User Account Management policy and log retention.
limitations: 4740 confirms lockout; Caller Computer Name is not proof of the human actor.
Preserve evidence and confirm account owner before unlocking/resetting.
next_checks: Correlate 4740 with preceding 4625 across relevant systems and DCs.
Investigate stale service/task credentials only when evidence ties them to the caller.
validation: After approved correction, verify lockout events stop and a controlled authorized sign-in succeeds.
rollback: Restore only the exact account/service configuration captured before the approved change.

candidates.version_scope: Windows Server; validate supported policy settings on deployed release
candidates.title: Configure and verify audit policy
candidates.applicability: Use to verify whether logon and account-management audit subcategories produce required events.
prerequisites: Know GPO owner/inheritance.
Approval before changing audit policy.
Assess event volume, capacity, forwarding and retention.
evidence: Presence or absence of expected event IDs
limitations: Absent event does not prove action did not occur; auditing may be disabled, filtered, overwritten or not forwarded.
Audit changes may increase event volume.
next_checks: Read effective policy before changes.
Stage policy on a test OU/system before broad rollout.
validation: Generate authorized test event and verify local plus central collection.
rollback: Restore captured pre-change GPO/audit values and verify effective policy.

candidates.version_scope: ESXi; only post-hardware-change or upgrade connectivity loss; verify exact release, NIC driver/firmware and vSAN topology
candidates.title: ESXi host network connectivity issues following hardware changes or upgrades
candidates.applicability: Host loses L3 connectivity to backend storage/vSAN VMkernel network after hardware change or ESXi upgrade and vmkping shows loss.
prerequisites: Maintenance window and physical network owner before cabling changes.
Identify vmnic/vmk mappings, VLANs and switch ports.
evidence: vmkping result with source vmk and payload/DF settings
limitations: Cable transposition is the cause for this documented scenario only; do not generalize.
Do not re-cable based only on ping failure.
next_checks: Inspect CDP/LLDP using supported esxcli diagnostics.
Compare switch MAC table, physical mapping and expected VLAN.
Use vmkping from intended VMkernel adapter after correction.
validation: Verify VMkernel-to-storage/vSAN reachability and datastore/path health on affected hosts.
rollback: Record original cable/port and switch configuration; restore known-good mapping if approved change worsens connectivity.

candidates.version_scope: Confirm article-supported builds and topology; article updated 2026-10-14
candidates.title: Troubleshooting virtual machine network connection issues
candidates.applicability: VM cannot reach selected IPs; inbound/outbound traffic absent; cross-VLAN or cross-host communication fails; or VM latency/connectivity is degraded.
prerequisites: Identify affected VM/host/port group/VDS/VLAN/source/destination and incident time.
evidence: vCenter and ESXi support bundles if issue is no longer present
limitations: Possible fault domains include guest, vSwitch, physical switch, routing, firewall and destination.
Do not infer a cause from symptoms alone; collect during incident where possible.
next_checks: Compare affected/unaffected VMs on same host/VLAN and across hosts.
Trace packet path before changing VLAN, port group or uplink.
validation: Repeat original source/destination connectivity test and verify unaffected traffic remains healthy.
rollback: Restore recorded port group, VLAN, uplink and security-policy values if an approved change regresses traffic.

candidates.version_scope: ESXi; validate FC/iSCSI/NFS protocol and array model/firmware compatibility
candidates.title: Identifying Fibre Channel, iSCSI, and NFS storage issues on ESXi hosts
candidates.applicability: ESXi cannot see targets/LUNs, initiators fail login, datastore will not mount, or mounted datastore cannot be written.
prerequisites: Coordinate storage and virtualization teams.
Record current array, fabric, host and path configuration before any changes.
limitations: Host symptom alone does not identify host, fabric, array, zoning, auth or protocol cause.
next_checks: Compare affected host to healthy peer on same fabric/LUN.
Validate physical links, target visibility and array mapping before changing ESXi config.
validation: Confirm expected targets/LUNs and paths healthy on intended hosts; use approved test datastore for controlled read/write check.
rollback: Restore recorded zoning, target mappings and path-policy settings if approved change regresses storage.

candidates.version_scope: VBR 13; verify build, chain type, repository and capacity-tier placement
candidates.title: Health Check for Backup Files
candidates.applicability: Periodic integrity verification of the latest restore point in a VM backup chain.
prerequisites: VBR 13 and repository access.
Understand chain type and maintenance schedule.
Avoid conflict with backup/restore jobs.
limitations: Verifies latest restore point, not all historical restore points.
Logical latest restore point can span multiple files.
Health check does not prove application recovery or business service recovery.
next_checks: Inspect configured health-check schedule.
Investigate repository/gateway capacity and contention if checks do not complete.
validation: Confirm health check passed for intended restore point; separately perform isolated workload recovery test.
rollback: Restore previous maintenance schedule if resource contention occurs; do not delete backup chains as troubleshooting.

candidates.version_scope: VBR 13; full recoverability requires supported Virtual Lab/Application Group configuration
candidates.title: SureBackup recovery verification
candidates.applicability: Verify a selected VM restore point can boot and pass configured checks in an isolated virtual lab.
prerequisites: Isolated Virtual Lab and Application Group as required.
Approved resource allocation and network isolation.
Application-specific checks defined by service owner.
limitations: Verification/content-scan-only mode is not full recoverability testing.
VM boot alone does not prove application consistency or business service recovery.
next_checks: Declare verification mode and exact checks actually run.
Keep recovered workloads isolated unless approved test design states otherwise.
validation: Verify VM boot and application-specific tests in isolated lab; retain report and isolation evidence.
rollback: Stop session and remove only temporary test artifacts using supported Veeam cleanup.

candidates.version_scope: Source page applies to build 13.1.1.18; verify installed build
candidates.title: Verifying Backups with SureBackup
candidates.applicability: Integrity verification or content scanning of VM restore points.
prerequisites: Confirm installed VBR build and workload support.
Verify AV/YARA integration and permissions when configured.
evidence: Infected restore-point and subsequent chain status
limitations: Does not certify RTO/RPO or application-level service recovery.
A failed verification can affect restore point and subsequent chain points.
next_checks: Inspect exact failed check and restore-point scope before repair or chain actions.
validation: Confirm intended verification checks pass and retain session report.
rollback: No universal rollback; do not clear infected state or alter chain without supported recovery procedure and preserved evidence.

candidates.version_scope: FortiOS 8.0.0 documentation; confirm installed build/model/feature visibility
candidates.title: Viewing event logs
candidates.applicability: Identify correct FortiGate event subtype; availability depends on enabled features and device capability.
prerequisites: Confirm FortiOS version, model, feature visibility and logging destination.
limitations: Not all subtypes are available by default; some depend on feature visibility or hardware.
Missing subtype does not prove event did not occur.
next_checks: Select relevant subtype and correlate with interface, routing, VPN or HA state.
validation: Confirm expected event type appears locally and in central logging.
rollback: No change prescribed; restore only separately approved logging/feature-visibility changes to captured values.

candidates.version_scope: FortiOS 8.0.0; verify NP6/NP7 hardware/offload applicability
candidates.title: Debugging the packet flow
candidates.applicability: Traffic is not entering, traversing or leaving FortiGate as expected and a narrowly filtered trace is required.
prerequisites: Authorized CLI and short diagnostic window.
Known source/destination/protocol/port filter.
Plan to stop trace and reset debug state.
evidence: Trace timestamp and bounded packet count
limitations: Debug flow can generate significant data and must not run longer than needed.
NP6/NP7 offloaded traffic may not appear; empty trace does not prove traffic absent.
Debug output may be forwarded to FortiAnalyzer/FortiCloud.
next_checks: Use narrowest filter and bounded trace count.
Stop trace when sufficient evidence is collected; account for offload.
validation: Repeat controlled traffic test and confirm expected route/policy/egress; verify application connectivity independently.
rollback: Stop trace, disable/reset debug, and restore temporary offload/policy settings to captured values.

candidates.version_scope: FortiOS 8.0.0; confirm HA topology, FGCP/FGSP and tunnel type
candidates.title: IPsec VPN in an HA environment
candidates.applicability: Investigate IPsec tunnel state in the documented HA topology.
prerequisites: Confirm HA mode/topology and peer roles.
Use read-only diagnostics before any tunnel synchronization or failover operation.
evidence: HA peer state and failover timeline
limitations: Established SA does not prove end-to-end application traffic flows.
Source example topology may differ from deployed environment.
next_checks: Compare SA state with counters and actual traffic tests.
Check HA role and sync before state-changing actions.
validation: Confirm tunnel state and bidirectional application test traffic after approved change.
rollback: No universal rollback; preserve prior tunnel/HA config and follow vendor-supported recovery for exact topology.

candidates.product: Windows Server Group Policy / Active Directory
candidates.version_scope: Windows Server; verify exact client/server OS build, GPO processing mode and domain topology
candidates.title: Applying Group Policy troubleshooting guidance — Event ID 1129
candidates.applicability: Use only when Microsoft-Windows-GroupPolicy Event ID 1129 records that Group Policy could not contact a domain controller due to network connectivity.
prerequisites: Identify client, domain controller, site/subnet, network path and whether failure is startup-only or persistent.
Do not assume LDAP 389 is the cause; Microsoft describes it as one documented scenario.
evidence: Client DNS resolver and DC discovery result
GPSvc debug log if enabled under an approved diagnostic plan
Firewall/router counters and GPO processing result
limitations: The article's blocked LDAP 389 example is one scenario, not a universal cause.
Network initialization race, DNS/DC discovery, routing, firewall/IPsec and DC availability must be distinguished.
next_checks: Verify DNS SRV/DC discovery and the selected DC.
Trace the actual path and confirm required directory-service ports from Microsoft documentation for the deployed configuration.
Correlate Netlogon 5719 and GroupPolicy events; check whether background refresh later succeeds.
validation: Run an authorized Group Policy refresh after the approved network correction.
Confirm successful processing in GPSvc logs and resultant policy; verify no unrelated DC traffic regressed.
rollback: Restore captured firewall/routing/GPO values if the approved change causes regression; remove temporary GPSvc debug settings after evidence capture.

candidates.version_scope: Windows Server; verify event provider and OS build because Event ID numbers are source-specific
candidates.title: Troubleshoot unexpected reboots using system event logs
candidates.applicability: Use EventLog 6005 as a boot-history marker and correlate with Kernel-General 12/13, Kernel-Power 41, User32 1074, EventLog 6008 and 6009.
prerequisites: Verify event provider/source, computer and timestamp; Event ID alone is not globally unique.
limitations: 6005 means the Event Log service started; it does not by itself prove why a reboot occurred or whether it was unexpected.
Use source/provider as well as numeric event ID.
next_checks: Build a chronological sequence across the listed events.
Distinguish planned shutdown (1074/13) from unexpected shutdown (41/6008) using the actual source and neighboring evidence.
validation: Confirm the reconstructed reboot timeline matches host uptime/boot time and an independent system or hypervisor record.
rollback: Read-only investigation; remove temporary event filters/export artifacts only.

candidates.product: VMware vSAN ESA / VMware Cloud Foundation
candidates.version_scope: Broadcom KB 442155: vSAN ESA snapshot CTK unlink failure; source states issue fixed in VCF 9.1. Confirm exact VCF/vSAN/ESXi build and support status.
candidates.domain: Changed Block Tracking file deletion / vSAN ESA snapshot cleanup
candidates.title: Snapshot usage on ESA cluster is very high due to CTK file deletion failure
candidates.applicability: Use only when vmware logs contain DISKLIB-CTK could not unlink tracking file / Could not delete change tracking file with result 2620 on vSAN ESA.
prerequisites: Confirm vSAN ESA topology, VCF/ESXi build, snapshot inventory and backup/replication activity.
Preserve vmware.log/vmware-*.log and snapshot/CTK file inventory before cleanup.
evidence: VM UUID, VMDK and CTK file paths
Concurrent backup/replication tasks and Broadcom support bundle
limitations: The KB is specific to vSAN ESA and states a fix in VCF 9.1; do not assume the fix applies to other vSAN/ESXi releases.
The article says existing orphaned snapshot cleanup should be handled with Broadcom Support; do not delete CTK/snapshot files manually.
next_checks: Check whether deployed VCF version includes the documented fix.
Escalate existing orphaned snapshot cleanup to Broadcom Support with logs and inventory.
validation: After vendor-approved correction, confirm CTK unlink errors stop and snapshot usage/chain state returns to expected values.
Run a controlled backup/replication and verify CBT/snapshot processing completes.
rollback: Do not manually remove CTK/snapshot files. Preserve original VM folder and snapshot metadata; follow Broadcom-directed recovery/rollback only.

candidates.version_scope: Broadcom KB 424591: ESXi 8.0 and vCenter 8.0. Validate exact build and storage type.
candidates.title: Reverting a virtual machine snapshot fails with A required file was not found
candidates.applicability: Use when snapshot revert reports InvalidSnapshotFormat and A required file was not found, and vpxd.log identifies a missing snapshot disk referenced by the target VM.
prerequisites: Confirm VM UUID, target snapshot, datastore availability and exact ESXi/vCenter versions.
Preserve VMX, VMSD, VMDK descriptors, snapshot tree and vpxd/hostd/vmware logs.
evidence: Full InvalidSnapshotFormat fault and NOTFOUND message
Target snapshot ID and VM UUID
Referenced snapshot-disk path and datastore mount state
Snapshot tree and descriptor/parent CID chain
Recent backup/restore or manual file movement timeline
limitations: A missing referenced snapshot disk is the documented cause for this specific error; do not generalize to all snapshot failures.
Restoring or moving VMDKs can affect snapshot-chain consistency and data integrity.
next_checks: Verify the referenced file path and datastore accessibility without changing files.
Compare VM configuration references with the actual snapshot disk inventory.
Engage Broadcom Support/storage owner before repairing the chain.
validation: After approved recovery, verify snapshot tree consistency, VM power state and application-level data integrity.
Run a controlled backup and confirm it completes without snapshot-chain errors.
rollback: Preserve a copy of the VM configuration and all disk descriptors before any approved repair; do not manually move/delete snapshot files without vendor-directed steps.

candidates.version_scope: Broadcom KB 343510 covers ESXi 6.x, 7.x and 8.x; verify exact build and storage topology.
candidates.identity: Snapshot consolidation A required file was not found
candidates.title: An error occurred while consolidating disks when deleting or consolidating snapshots
candidates.applicability: Use when snapshot delete/consolidation reports A required file was not found, missing virtual disk or snapshot disk, or related parent disk errors.
prerequisites: Record VM power state, snapshot tree, datastore health/capacity and exact error.
Preserve all VM disk descriptors, logs and backup-chain state before remediation.
evidence: vCenter task error and VM UUID
Referenced VMDK/snapshot paths and parent CID
limitations: A missing virtual disk/snapshot file at the configured path is one documented cause; lock, busy-disk, I/O and parent-CID mismatch are separate cases.
Do not delete files or consolidate manually without identifying the exact failure branch.
next_checks: Match the exact error to the KB cause/resolution table.
Verify referenced files exist and datastores are mounted at the expected paths.
Use vendor support for uncertain or inconsistent snapshot chains.
validation: Confirm snapshot delete/consolidation completes and VM disk chain remains consistent.
Run application-level checks and a controlled backup.
rollback: Preserve VM folder, descriptors and snapshot metadata; use an approved backup/restore or vendor-guided recovery plan.

candidates.version_scope: VBR 13 REST API 1.3-rev2; verify installed API version and role permissions.
candidates.identity: VBR session result Failed / task-session log
candidates.title: Veeam Backup & Replication 13 REST API — Get Session Logs
candidates.applicability: Use when a Veeam job/replica session is marked Failed but the top-level status does not contain the underlying task failure.
prerequisites: Authorized VBR API role (Backup Administrator/Operator/Restore Operator/Backup Viewer or approved custom role).
Capture session UUID and exact VBR/API build.
evidence: Session UUID, job UUID, name and creation/end timestamps
Failed task title/description and preceding warning/success records
limitations: A generic Failed session status is an outcome, not a root cause.
API role and version constraints apply; task-session and session logs are distinct endpoints.
next_checks: Retrieve session detail and full ordered logs for the exact failed session.
Identify the first failing task and correlate with VMware/Hyper-V/storage/network evidence.
validation: After the underlying cause is corrected, run a controlled job and verify session result plus all task logs are successful.
rollback: Read-only investigation; no backup-chain or job configuration changes are prescribed by this API reference.

candidates.version_scope: FortiOS 7.6.0 log-message reference; confirm exact FortiOS build and traffic-log schema.
candidates.identity: FortiGate logid 0000000013 / type traffic / subtype forward
candidates.title: Log message fields — FortiGate / FortiOS 7.6.0
candidates.applicability: Use when logid 0000000013 appears in a FortiGate traffic forward log.
prerequisites: Preserve the complete raw log; confirm type=traffic and subtype=forward.
Verify action, policyid, interfaces, addresses and FortiOS build.
evidence: proto, service, sessionid, duration, sent/received bytes
UTM action and security fields if present
limitations: Log ID 0000000013 identifies a forward traffic log, not an allow/deny verdict by itself.
The action field determines interpretation: Deny is policy blocked; Start is a session-start log that means allowed; other action values describe how an allowed session closed.
next_checks: Interpret action with policyid and direction; do not infer denial from logid alone.
Correlate with policy/config change events and packet-flow evidence when traffic is unexpected.
validation: Compare the expected test flow with raw log action, policy and byte counters in both directions.
rollback: Read-only log interpretation; do not change firewall policy solely because this log ID is present.

candidates.version_scope: FortiGate configuration event log; source article does not specify a single FortiOS build, so verify the installed firmware and schema.
candidates.title: Difference between logid 0100044547 and 0100044546 when FortiGate configuration changes
candidates.applicability: Use when FortiGate system event log contains logid 0100044547 indicating an object attribute configured event.
prerequisites: Preserve raw event and verify FortiGate device/firmware.
Confirm authorized administrator, change ticket and management interface.
limitations: 0100044547 indicates an object attribute was created/modified/deleted; it does not by itself prove malicious or unauthorized activity.
Interpret action and cfgpath/cfgattr; the change may be an approved administrator action.
next_checks: Match user/UI/action/object path to approved change records.
Compare before/after configuration through approved FortiGate configuration history.
validation: Confirm the final configuration matches the approved change and expected traffic/security behavior.
rollback: Use the approved FortiGate configuration revision/backup and change rollback procedure; do not revert configuration from a single log event.
